title: Regional pronunciation
intro: How often US and UK English differ, how well each way of generating a UK pronunciation matches real UK dictionary entries, and what the differences look like word by word.
diffTitle: How often common words differ, US against UK
diffTip: 6,104 words in the 8,000 most common that appear in both WikiPron lists, mapped to our sound symbols. Best matching pronunciation pair per word.
methodsTitle: Ways to produce a UK pronunciation
methodsNote: Match means the generated pronunciation equals at least one WikiPron UK pronunciation for the word. Lenient, because WikiPron lists several variants per word.

copy the US pronunciation: Use the US dictionary entry unchanged.
Right for the 80% of words that do not differ.
drop the r after a vowel: Remove r unless a vowel follows (car, but very keeps it).
Turn final unstressed ER into a schwa.
Vowel plus r becomes a long vowel or a centring glide (near, square).
plus yod and the BATH vowel: Add y before a stressed oo after t, d, n, s, z, th, l when the spelling has u or ew (tune, new).
Change short a to the long a in bath, dance, answer.
plus weak vowels chosen from the spellin: An unstressed vowel spelled i, e or y becomes IH in the UK where the US has schwa (business, women, started).
This is the one rule that needs the alignment.
eSpeak, UK voice (from spelling, no dict: No dictionary. eSpeak writes the UK pronunciation from the spelling with its own rules and exceptions.
reference: eSpeak US voice against WikiP: The same test for the US voice, so the UK result can be read fairly.
